subject: Evals: rollout acceptance & rollback guardrails for March A/B
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft prompt set + ask: acceptance thresholds and rollback plan

Team — attaching the initial prompt_set for the Acme March A/B (eval_prompt_set_v1.csv). Goal: validate that the new model family (millennium-v2-q4) does not regress on the core newsroom prompts and passes the new factuality checks.

Ask: can product/ops agree on a concise acceptance criteria we can gate on in CI? My proposal (quick):
- P0: no >1% drop in exact-title-match on headline generation across the 2k seed prompts.
- P1: mean factuality score (our hallucination classifier) ≥ 0.87.
- P2: toxicity regression < 0.2 abs delta.
- P3: latency p95 must remain ≤ 450ms for 512 tokens when served in dedicated pool.

Also attaching a matrix (ab_plan_matrix.xlsx) with proposed traffic splits: 5% canary → 25% expand → 50% full. I need approval on: thresholds above, canary window (I suggest 48h per step), and whether we require an immediate auto-rollback trigger for any P0 or P1 failure.

Context: Acme is sensitive to headline accuracy (they flagged a prior small hallucination in Jan). They expect an explicit rollback plan.

Next steps I expect: product writes acceptance criteria language we can embed in the CI gate; ops confirms rollout windows and rollback automation; research finalizes the evaluation scripts and runs the first pass.

— Dev
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft prompt set + ask: acceptance thresholds and rollback plan

Thanks — good start. A few clarifications and proposals from product's side:

1) Acceptance language we will codify (CI-friendly):
- Pass condition = all P0 AND P1 AND P2 AND P3 must be satisfied. If any P0 breach occurs, fail fast and block rollout.
- P0 = headline-title-identity: exact-title-match drop <= 1% (relative) across canonical seed set (2,000 prompts).
- P1 = factuality: mean hallucination-score >= 0.87 AND no more than 0.5% of responses flagged as high-confidence hallucinations.
- P2 = safety: toxicity delta <= 0.2 absolute compared to baseline.
- P3 = perf: p95 latency <= 450ms as you proposed.

2) Canary windows: I agree 48h for the initial 5% canary but recommend we add an automated metrics check at 12h and 36h (so we don't wait full 48h to detect a sharp regression). If any check fails, the canary auto-rollbacks to baseline.

3) Rollback automation: ops to confirm whether we can wire the CI gate to a single API call that flips the routing policy (preferred), otherwise manual rollback with a documented playbook.

4) Acceptance docs: I'll author a short acceptance criteria doc and link it into the drive folder.

Marissa — tagging you for SLA/ops constraints and Connor for routing/traffic toggles. Evelyn — can you confirm the eval script inputs and whether the prompt set needs any augmentation for the hallucination detectors?

Thanks — Laura
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft prompt set + ask: acceptance thresholds and rollback plan

On the ops side:
- We can wire an automated rollback for a canary if the CI job posts a failure to SUP-3421 (Jira). That's our preferred path; Connor will need to add the playbook hook.
- Canary timing OK: 5% for 48h with 12h/36h gates is reasonable. Note that Acme's traffic spike window is 09:00–11:00 PST weekdays — suggest avoiding canary expansion across that window.
- Perf: the p95 target is achievable if we pin instance types to the existing dedicated pool (no autoscaling during canary).

Attachments: I've uploaded a concise rollback_playbook.md to the drive with step-by-step roles/responsibilities (review and confirm).

Operational asks for product/research: please include a small subset (n=200) of production stems that simulate the high-traffic 09:00–11:00 PST period so we can run spike testing during canary. Otherwise the perf numbers are optimistic.

— Marissa
Head of Platform Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft prompt set + ask: acceptance thresholds and rollback plan

Thanks — I've started a dry run (local eval harness) against eval_prompt_set_v1.csv. Quick notes:
- The hallucination classifier thresholds need a tiny adjustment for this seed set; with the current model a lot of borderline factuality hits are right on the 0.87 mark. Proposal: keep mean >= 0.87 but also require that the 90th-percentile hallucination score <= 0.92 to catch tail degradation.
- A/B plan: for metrics we should report both absolute and relative deltas for the core metrics (exact-title-match, factuality, toxicity, latency). In the dashboard: show smoothed 6-hour deltas and a 95% CI.
- Acceptance automation: I will add an eval pipeline step that emits a single JSON gate result (pass/fail) plus a short summary (metrics diffs and sample counterexamples) to the Drive folder. That JSON file can be polled by SUP-3421 and then trigger rollback.

Small forward: I'm forwarding an internal note I sent last week with examples of 'headline hallucinations' to make sure we're aligned on what constitutes a P1 failure.
